kind: local agent (Python, Nous Hermes Agent); bin is a bash wrapper around ~/.hermes/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes

binary.sha256_note: binary is a wrapper/entry script, so this sha256 covers only the script text, not the interpreter or the package it launches

version_raw: Python: 3.11.15 | OpenAI SDK: 2.24.0 | Update available: 12642 commits behind — run 'hermes update'
model_route: OpenRouter via --provider openrouter -m <model>; key read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY env
isolation: HERMES_HOME={HOME} (fresh home, own config.yaml/auth.json/state.db); user's ~/.hermes untouched

one_shot.method: spawn argv, 120s hard timeout (SIGTERM then SIGKILL on the process group); true iff the process exits by itself and stdout+stderr (with every echo of the prompt text removed) contains PONG

file_edits.method: after the run, read <cwd>/PROBE.txt from the fresh temp dir; true iff it exists and equals "probe-ok" (one trailing newline tolerated)

tool_use.method: true iff stdout+stderr (prompt echoes removed) contains TOOL-OK-4471 (as specified). Caveat: the token is in the prompt, so a model that merely repeats it would pass; corroborated with (a) tool-call event lines matched by tool_call_regex and (b) the file_edits result, which is on-disk proof of tool execution
tool_use.note: token present; tool-call lines in transcript: 0 []; file_edits corroboration: true. -z one-shot prints only the final answer, so tool calls are not visible in the transcript; file_edits (file on disk) is the hard evidence.

browser.method: true iff stdout+stderr contains "Example Domain"; the mechanism (real browser vs plain HTTP fetch) is inferred from tool names in the transcript, which is only visible when the harness streams tool events
browser.note: title reported; mechanism: not visible in output; tool lines: []

sandbox.method: compare reported hostname/pwd with this machine (hostname=<hostname>.local, cwd=<temp dir>); a different hostname or a container-style path means sandboxed
sandbox.note:
reported this machine's hostname (<hostname>.local) and the real temp cwd, so tools run directly on the host. tail: "hostname:
<hostname>.local

pwd:
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-<user>/c7fd89f2-986d-4551-b6d0-4f5a66a90bb8/scratchpad/abilities/hermes/probes/sandbox"

mcp_client.method: isolated config registers Timmy's stdio MCP server; true iff the reply contains a value only the real timmy_env_lock result has (OS build id or a tool sha256 prefix obtained by calling the server directly first), or the tool name plus os/arch fields plus a visible tool-call event

argv: Reply with exactly the word PONG and nothing else
Create a file named PROBE.txt in the current directory containing exactly the text probe-ok, then stop.
Run the shell command `echo TOOL-OK-4471` and report its output verbatim.
Fetch https://example.com and report the exact page title.
Run the shell commands `hostname` and `pwd` and report both verbatim.
Call the MCP tool timmy_env_lock and paste its raw JSON result.

notes: removed isolated-home credential file after run: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-<user>/c7fd89f2-986d-4551-b6d0-4f5a66a90bb8/scratchpad/abilities/hermes/home/auth.json
